text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia and workers' union acting secretary-general Sidi Said to hold joint news conference on the impact of a minimum wage hike.

- French aviation authorities dismiss British Airways' concerns over the resumption of flights by Air Algerie at Paris airport. French Versailles court expected to deliver verdict on British Airways allegations of insecurity stemming from Air Algerie's presence at the airport. The British airline diverted some flights away from Charles de Gaulle airport after French authorities last week allowed Air Algerie to resume operations.
- Algeria posts a $1.7 billion trade balance surplus in the first quarter of 1997.
- Hundreds of women, braving taboos in a male-dominated society, stand as candidates for the 380-seat National Assembly election in June 5.
- U.N. envoy James Baker meets Polisario leaders to discuss the dispute in Western Sahara. The Polisario Front announces it is to free 85 Moroccan prisoners of war as Baker arrives.
